claim: Ed Belfour stopped 32 of 33 shots for the Panthers while Jocelyn Thibault stopped 39 of the 41 he faced.

passages.text: The Pittsburgh Penguins won an exciting game Friday in Miami, as they defeated the Florida Panthers. The Penguins, just off of a 16 game winning streak after dropping one to the New York Islanders on Monday, had some goalie controversy as to who will start the game. Penguins coach Michel Therrien had said that he was unhappy with the play of goalie Marc-Andre Fleury against the Islanders. As a result of this, goalie Jocelyn Thibault got the nod to start for the Pens on Thursday. There was also a goalie problem for the Panthers, as Alex Auld (Panthers starting goalie) had suffered an injury in a previous game and was out for the night. Instead, they started the old veteran Ed Belfour, who did a good job, stoping the puck 39 of the 41 shots he faced, which is a solid outing for any goalie. But it would be Jocelyn Thibault who outdid him, stopping 32 of 33 shots on goal. Goal scoring was rather low, though, with Jordan Staal (Powerplay) and Colby Armstrong (Game winner, Overtime) scoring for the Penguins and Juraj Kolník scoring for the Panthers. Assists were credited to Evgeni Malkin, Sidney Crosby, Maxime Talbot, and Ryan Whitney for the Pens and Chris Gratton and Bryan Allen for the Panthers. The Three Stars of the game were given to Colby Armstrong (First Star), Jocelyn Thibault (Second Star),and Ed Belfour (Third Star). All in all, this game was well played and was a solid win for the streaking Penguins. Pittsburgh will travel across the state to face the surging Tampa Bay Lightning this Sunday.

The Sudanese Government said it will not hand over 51 suspects named by the UN for war crimes in the Darfur region. The sealed list, presented to the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Tuesday, was drawn up following an investigation by the UN into claims of killings, torture and rape committed by Government forces and militias in the Darfur region. Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir, backed by huge protests against the UN in Sudan's capital of Khartoum, snubbed the UN resolution which was passed last week to bring suspects to trial before the court. Omar al-Bashir explained that he "shall never hand any Sudanese national to a foreign court". [1] ICC's chief prosecutor Luis Moreno Ocampo said, "Now, we have a common task to end the culture of impunity," upon receiving the list of suspects at the UN headquarters in New York. He continued: "I will closely monitor ongoing crimes in Darfur as well as efforts to prevent and stop them". The Darfur case is expected to demonstrate the effectiveness of the ICC, whose purpose is to try alleged genocide, war crimes and mass human rights violations criminals. As the ICC, based in the Hague, received thousands of pages of evidence collected by UN investigators, Sudanese protesters descended upon the gates of the UN compound in Khartoum, fiercely criticising the UN's involvement in the Darfur conflict. [2] "We are coming here to say to America 'no' to these orders. We are not people who have to listen to orders from anybody except the Sudan," one demonstrator told the BBC. Stating that it will prosecute suspects itself, Sudan's government earlier described the UN's decision to try individuals allegedly linked to the atrocities committed in Darfur as "unfair, ill-advised and narrow-minded". [3] The UN has since said it hoped the Sudanese Government would cooperate before indictments and arrest warrants are issued, and the UN understood that Sudanese rebels will surrender to the court if they are indicted. [4] According to the UN, at least 180,000 people have died and more than two million have fled the region since the conflict between black African rebels and Arab militia began two years ago.

passages.text: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most prevalent disorders affecting women. The status of PCOS research in sub-Saharan Africa is unknown, where non-communicable diseases are prevalent but often underrecognized. To assess current knowledge about PCOS in sub-Saharan Africa and identify gaps in the literature. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and African Journals Online through 9 August 2026 to identify original studies on PCOS in sub-Saharan Africa. Original research studies involving sub-Saharan African populations, without age-related constraints, were eligible. We excluded non-original studies and studies that did not focus on PCOS. Three independent reviewers (S.H., M.A., and C.C.M.) performed the searches. Of 1973 retrieved records, 40 studies met the inclusion criteria, predominantly from Nigeria, with additional contributions from South Africa, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, Benin, Kenya, and Ethiopia. No population-based prevalence studies were identified; however, 13 studies reported PCOS prevalence, mostly in clinically selected populations. PCOS remains understudied in sub-Saharan Africa, with substantial gaps in population-based epidemiology, diagnostic practices, phenotype distribution, management, and metabolic outcomes. Addressing these gaps through larger, well-designed studies is critical to accurately assess the disease burden, inform clinical guidelines, and optimize management strategies. Additionally, overcoming barriers such as cultural attitudes, cost, and limited accessibility to diagnostic tools and treatment options remains essential to improving PCOS care and research across the region.PROSPERO registration ID CRD420250649730 - 13 March 2025.

claim: The network meta-analysis established that self-directed activities improve older adults' quality of life more than social activities do.

passages.text: Meaningful activity participation may support healthy aging and quality of life (QoL) in community-dwelling older adults. We compared interaction-based social, exercise-based physical, and self-directed individual activities. Thirteen English- and Korean-language databases were searched through May 2026 for RCTs of community-dwelling older adults with a study-sample mean or median age ≥65 years. Interventions were classified using a theoretically informed operational framework. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2. Pairwise and Bayesian network meta-analyses estimated standardized mean differences (SMDs); certainty was assessed using GRADE, with SUCRA rankings considered secondary. Seventy-one RCTs (12,159 participants) were included. The overall pairwise effect favored activity-based interventions (SMD=0.59, 95% CI 0.45-0.73), but heterogeneity was substantial and the prediction interval crossed the null; certainty was very low. Category-specific pairwise estimates were 0.68 (0.27-1.08) for self-directed, 0.61 (0.43-0.78) for physical, and 0.46 (0.21-0.72) for social activities, all with very-low-certainty evidence. In the network meta-analysis, low-certainty evidence suggested that all three categories may improve QoL versus no treatment: self-directed SMD=0.78 (95% CrI 0.25-1.32; SUCRA 82.5%), physical 0.73 (0.46-1.00; 79.6%), and social 0.40 (0.11-0.69; 37.6%). Excluding high-risk studies yielded an overall pairwise estimate of 0.53 (0.37-0.69); the estimate for physical activities remained 0.61, whereas the estimates for social and self-directed activities were 0.43 and 0.45. Evidence does not establish superiority of one activity category. Findings remain limited by heterogeneity, risk of bias, potential publication bias, and sparse direct active comparisons. Comparative rankings should be considered hypothesis-generating, and higher-quality head-to-head trials are needed.

Previous syntheses included broader age ranges and heterogeneous exercise classifications, leaving uncertainty about comparative effects across exercise modalities in pediatric populations. This review examined whether exercise modalities differ in their effects on visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and waist circumference (WC) in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity, and whether any modality shows superior effectiveness. Randomized and partially randomized controlled trials were identified from PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, and CNKI. VAT and WC were primary outcomes; SAT, body fat percentage, BMI, body weight, fat mass, and VO₂max were secondary outcomes. Hedges' g was synthesized using three-level random-effects models to accommodate dependent effect sizes within studies. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane tool. Twenty-one trials involving 1,754 participants were included. Exercise interventions were associated with lower VAT (g = -0.725, 95% CI [-1.120, -0.330], p < 0.001) and WC (g = -0.692, 95% CI [-0.984, -0.400], p < 0.001). HIIT showed the largest VAT point estimate (g = -1.332, 95% CI [-1.874, -0.789]), but between-modality differences were not significant for VAT ( p = 0.116) or WC ( p = 0.184). Prediction intervals for both primary outcomes crossed the null, indicating uncertainty across study settings. Secondary outcomes generally favored exercise. Exercise-based interventions were associated with reductions in VAT and WC, but current evidence does not establish the superiority of any single modality. Although HIIT showed the largest VAT point estimate, non-significant between-modality tests and prediction intervals crossing the null preclude firm conclusions about an optimal exercise modality. CRD420261431627, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261431627.

label: contradicted

evidence.quote: Evidence does not establish superiority of one activity category
low-certainty evidence suggested that all three categories may improve QoL versus no treatment

rationale: Self-directed activities did have the larger estimate (SMD 0.78 against 0.40), but the authors say in so many words that the evidence does not establish the superiority of one category, and the network estimates are low certainty. Stating it as established is what the abstract denies.

Hedges' g was synthesized using three-level random-effects models to accommodate dependent effect sizes within studies. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane tool. Twenty-one trials involving 1,754 participants were included. Exercise interventions were associated with lower VAT (g = -0.725, 95% CI [-1.120, -0.330], p < 0.001) and WC (g = -0.692, 95% CI [-0.984, -0.400], p < 0.001). HIIT showed the largest VAT point estimate (g = -1.332, 95% CI [-1.874, -0.789]), but between-modality differences were not significant for VAT ( p = 0.116) or WC ( p = 0.184). Prediction intervals for both primary outcomes crossed the null, indicating uncertainty across study settings. Secondary outcomes generally favored exercise. Exercise-based interventions were associated with reductions in VAT and WC, but current evidence does not establish the superiority of any single modality. Although HIIT showed the largest VAT point estimate, non-significant between-modality tests and prediction intervals crossing the null preclude firm conclusions about an optimal exercise modality. passages.text: The Sudanese Government said it will not hand over 51 suspects named by the UN for war crimes in the Darfur region. The sealed list, presented to the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Tuesday, was drawn up following an investigation by the UN into claims of killings, torture and rape committed by Government forces and militias in the Darfur region. Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir, backed by huge protests against the UN in Sudan's capital of Khartoum, snubbed the UN resolution which was passed last week to bring suspects to trial before the court. Omar al-Bashir explained that he "shall never hand any Sudanese national to a foreign court". [1] ICC's chief prosecutor Luis Moreno Ocampo said, "Now, we have a common task to end the culture of impunity," upon receiving the list of suspects at the UN headquarters in New York. He continued: "I will closely monitor ongoing crimes in Darfur as well as efforts to prevent and stop them". The Darfur case is expected to demonstrate the effectiveness of the ICC, whose purpose is to try alleged genocide, war crimes and mass human rights violations criminals. As the ICC, based in the Hague, received thousands of pages of evidence collected by UN investigators, Sudanese protesters descended upon the gates of the UN compound in Khartoum, fiercely criticising the UN's involvement in the Darfur conflict. [2] "We are coming here to say to America 'no' to these orders. We are not people who have to listen to orders from anybody except the Sudan," one demonstrator told the BBC. Stating that it will prosecute suspects itself, Sudan's government earlier described the UN's decision to try individuals allegedly linked to the atrocities committed in Darfur as "unfair, ill-advised and narrow-minded". [3] The UN has since said it hoped the Sudanese Government would cooperate before indictments and arrest warrants are issued, and the UN understood that Sudanese rebels will surrender to the court if they are indicted. [4] According to the UN, at least 180,000 people have died and more than two million have fled the region since the conflict between black African rebels and Arab militia began two years ago.

Declining atmospheric sulfur (S) deposition makes S an emerging limiting macronutrient for plants, yet the stability and dynamics of soil organic S-the largest terrestrial S pool supplying plant-available sulfate via mineralization-remain unclear. Across North American soils, total organic S is dominated by mineral-associated organic S (MAOS; 61% ± 26%); this pool is stabilized by mineral protection but saturates at ~600 μg S/g soil. Compared with particulate organic S (POS), which is relatively labile and does not saturate, MAOS is more decomposed, chemically diverse, and climate-sensitive. Higher temperature accelerates S mineralization in both pools, but their ability to supply available S varies with moisture regime because MAOS stabilizes in wetter soils while POS remains labile. This continental-scale reassessment of the soil S cycle reveals that secondary minerals play a dual role in soil S cycling by stabilizing organic S and retaining sulfate, providing a mechanistic basis for nutrient management and carbon sequestration in response to climate change in an S-scarce future.
